title: Meta flags a Raebareli 18-year-old's Instagram suicide post at 8:58 pm; Uttar Pradesh Police reach him within 12 minutes after he took rat poison, and he is treated and stable
summary: Meta's suicide detection and review system flagged an 18-year-old's Instagram post; Raebareli police reached him within 12 minutes, and he was treated after taking rat poison.
account: On 29 March 2026 an 18-year-old class 12 student from Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, texted his girlfriend “Alvida” after a breakup. He lived within the Mill Area police station limits. He also posted a suicide video on Instagram with rat poison and messages of intent. At about 8:58 pm Meta flagged the content and emailed an alert to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters. The center traced his mobile number and location and alerted Raebareli police. A police team reached his home within 12 minutes and found him in severe distress, with an empty rat-poison packet nearby. Police and family took him to a nearby hospital, where he was treated. On 1 April 2026 police said that he was stable. Similar rescues after Meta alerts followed in Meerut in June 2026 and in Gorakhpur in October 2026. The Times of India reported on 22 October 2026 that Uttar Pradesh Police say that they saved more than 4,000 lives from 1 January 2023 to 10 October 2026 by responding to alerts linked to suicide-related posts. According to Decode, the arrangement with Meta has been in place since 2022.
purpose: Meta's detection and review system is built to find posts and live videos that indicate suicide or self-injury risk. It routes them to trained reviewers and, in imminent cases, contacts local authorities. The Uttar Pradesh Police Social Media Center exists to act on those alerts. This rescue is that purpose.
system: Meta's suicide and self-injury detection and review pipeline on Instagram, with email alerts to the Uttar Pradesh Police Social Media Center at DGP headquarters
deployer: Meta Platforms with the Uttar Pradesh Police Social Media Center (Decode: Uttar Pradesh has been part of Meta's suicide-prevention program since 2022)
taxonomy_note: A suicide intervention; Trustible's only health type is physical health.

ratings.reason: An 18-year-old who had taken rat poison was reached within 12 minutes of Meta's 8:58 pm alert. He was treated in hospital and reported stable. Officials said even a slight delay could have been fatal. No clinician is quoted and the rodenticide is not identified. The life-saving reading rests on the police account.

ai_role.statement: Police say Meta flagged the Instagram post at about 8:58 pm on 29 March and emailed the Uttar Pradesh Police Social Media Center. No source says whether Meta's classifier or a user report started the review. Decode reports that UP alerts arise from “artificial intelligence systems or user reports” reviewed by Meta staff. Everything after the email was human work. The center traced the phone number and location. Raebareli police reached the home in 12 minutes on the DGP's instructions, and a hospital treated him.

brief: The Raebareli rescue preceded a similar rescue in Meerut in June 2026, both under an arrangement in which Meta has alerted the Uttar Pradesh Police since 2022.[1] On 29 March 2026 an 18-year-old posted a suicide video on Instagram. Meta flagged it at about 8:58 pm and emailed the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters, which traced his phone number and location and alerted Raebareli police. A team reached his home within 12 minutes and found an empty rat-poison packet, and police and family took him to hospital; on 1 April 2026 police said that he was stable.[2] No source says whether Meta’s classifier or a user report first flagged the post.[3] No clinician is quoted and the type of rat poison is not reported, so the claim that his life was saved rests on the police account.[4] Meta’s figure for faster escalation is self-reported and dates from November 2017, when the company said that reports accelerated by pattern recognition were escalated to local authorities twice as quickly as other reports.[5]

display.answer: The case reports of 1 April 2026 rest on statements by Uttar Pradesh Police, and two of them carry the same IANS story. Decode describes how the arrangement with Meta works, and Meta's newsroom posts of 2017 and 2018 describe its detection system. The count of more than 4,000 lives saved is the police's own figure, reported by The Times of India on 22 October 2026.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Meta's suicide detection and review system flagged an 18-year-old's Instagram post; Raebareli police reached him within 12 minutes, and he was treated after taking rat poison.
fields.account: On 29 March 2026 an 18-year-old class 12 student from Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, texted his girlfriend “Alvida” after a breakup. He lived within the Mill Area police station limits. He also posted a suicide video on Instagram with rat poison and messages of intent. At about 8:58 pm Meta flagged the content and emailed an alert to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters. The center traced his mobile number and location and alerted Raebareli police. A police team reached his home within 12 minutes and found him in severe distress, with an empty rat-poison packet nearby. Police and family took him to a nearby hospital, where he was treated. On 1 April 2026 police said that he was stable. Similar rescues after Meta alerts followed in Meerut in June 2026 and in Gorakhpur in October 2026. The Times of India reported on 22 October 2026 that Uttar Pradesh Police say that they saved more than 4,000 lives from 1 January 2023 to 10 October 2026 by responding to alerts linked to suicide-related posts. According to Decode, the arrangement with Meta has been in place since 2022.
